items.description: Inventory of pipeline types: every kind of pipeline the estate runs, and for each topic the variants in use today — built from the jobs of report.md Appendix A and the clones. Every Appendix A job belongs to exactly one type, except the jobs of the five ModernAppTemplate repos (DHCPApp, ElectronicsInventory, IoTSupport, ZigbeeControl, FieldnotesApp), which are listed as skipped, with that reason (ruling F2). The inventory sits where the migration slice can work from it.

items.description: Rulings page: one proposed rule plus an example per topic — stage naming, stage granularity, checkout, pod definition, secrets and `withVault` scope, timeouts, `post`/`notify`, file naming and headers, and when code goes into the library — in the slice folder. "Stage granularity and the library rule are judgment calls, so Claude doesn't settle them alone." The operator rules before the guide is written: the rulings stand in plan.md's Requirements / rulings before the first guide page is committed.

A dedicated section on stage labels ("Please have a dedicated section for labeling stages. I find these very messy and all over the place."). It sits next to the section on stage granularity, not inside it.

The cookbook — the style guide itself, strict ("I want it to be followed strictly"), with examples, covering every pipeline type: rules written as MUSTs with the reason for each, one complete reference Jenkinsfile per pipeline type of the inventory, a short recipe per topic, and declarative only (J08 is "migrate all").

"Every example passes the declarative linter": each example, an excerpt inside the complete file it is cut from, passes the controller's full check at `/pipeline-model-converter/validate`, and the published example is byte for byte the one checked.

items.area: R4 — The rulings the guide carries
items.description: The guide carries exactly the rulings of review plan §4 and the operator's rulings from the rulings page: J24 (`checkout scm` for the job's own repo), J23 (the one load line, floating on `main`, no pin), J01 (the job-properties block and its placement, in declarative `options {}`/`triggers {}`; retention is the global build discarder, so files declare none), J08 (declarative), J11/J12 (the standard timeout, and only the exceptions the rulings page settles, ruling F5; the iac files' 4-hour backstop with a `post { aborted }` notify), J17 (`withVault` scope), J19 (the iac dev-stage duplication is deliberate: those files stay self-contained), the §6a result (what a new repo needs for its push hook), non-secret settings inline rather than as global env vars (Q6; `HA_URL` is the ruled exception, and endpoints never go into OpenBao), `notify` use, `Jenkinsfile.*` naming, and header comments.

items.area: R4 — Stage generators and computed triggers
items.description: The guide has a recipe for each pipeline that generates stages or computes its triggers: `DockerImages/Jenkinsfile` (a stage per image variant), `Intercom/Jenkinsfile` (a stage pair per hardware version) and `Architecture/Jenkinsfile` (triggers computed from YAML, which `triggers {}` cannot express).

items.area: R4 — The pod helper (033 close-out B3)
items.description: The guide describes the pod helper as it is — the global var `podYaml`, called as `podYaml(templates: [...], images: [...])` inside `agent { kubernetes { ... } }` — and states the map form of an `images:` entry with an explicit container `name:`.
evidence: /work/JenkinsPipelineUtils/vars/podYaml.groovy exists as its own var at d9ff168

items.area: R5 — When code goes into the library
items.description: When code goes into the library ("And when do we put something into the utility library."): the guide gives a decision test, with examples from the estate — J14/J15/J16 are accepted helpers, and J19 was ruled against ("Keep the duplication; the style guide says it is deliberate").

items.area: R6 — Docs site source and build
items.description: Docs site: source in `JenkinsPipelineUtils/docs/`, built with MkDocs + Material (ruling D2) on KubeCoder's manual as the basis, "including its LLM support": `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and a per-page `.md` copy for every page, plus the validation settings under which the build fails `--strict` on an orphaned page, a missing target, an absolute link or a broken anchor. The strict build runs in the library's `kc project test`.

"Hostname: pipelines.home/docs, with an index page at /." The site image serves a small landing page at `/` that links to the docs, and the docs under `/docs/`. The name is LAN-only, published by the Service annotations with a step-ca certificate, and the image's nginx config passes `nginx -t` at build time.

items.area: R6 / D6 — The site is live
items.description: Once the ArgoCDDeploy push lands, Argo syncs the `pipelines` app on its own, with no Argo action by anyone (ruling D6). `https://pipelines.home/` then answers with the landing page, and `https://pipelines.home/docs/` and its `llms.txt` answer with the guide, when fetched from a KubeCoder environment. The site is served from the image tag that the latest site build pinned in PipelinesDeploy.

The site is served as its own small app, the way charts.home is served (ruling D1). The library's Jenkinsfile follows the guide, and a job created through the API runs it. Its first build from the pushed library is green: it pushes the site image to `registry:5000` and writes the image pin into PipelinesDeploy's prd values. The job builds and publishes the site only; slice 033's ruling that the library's tests get no Jenkins job stands.
evidence: /work/JenkinsPipelineUtils/.kubecoder/project.yaml:3 ("No Jenkins job builds this repo." — true before this slice)

items.area: R6 / D1 / D6 — Deploy repo and registrations
items.description: PipelinesDeploy is shaped like ChartsDeploy, and its `kc project test` is green, with the placeholder manifest replaced by the real one. `AaC/PipelinesDeploy`'s first build is green and archives the producer's artifact. ArgoCDDeploy's registry carries the app's prd stage, auto-synced from the start, the way charts is registered (ruling D6). The producer is registered in Architecture's `pipeline-producers.yaml`, and that commit reaches `main` only after the AaC job's first green build.

J22's docs half: library reference pages on the site, kept next to `vars/`, including the pod helper slice 033 added. There is one hand-written page for every global var, and a library test in `kc project test` fails when a var has no page. That failure has been witnessed, not assumed.
evidence: /work/JenkinsPipelineUtils/vars/ at d9ff168: cicd, containerTemplates, gitUtils, helmCharts, kubectl, notify, podYaml, utils (.groovy)

items.description: The skill ("Instead I want a skill.") is in KubeCoderConfig's `kubecoder` plugin (ruling D3). "The skill is itself still a reference to the online docs": it carries the guide's hard rules and links to the site. It follows that repo's conventions — the plugin `version` is bumped in the same commit and the Markdown passes the repo's Prettier check, run through `modern-app` (ruling D5) — and it is pushed to KubeCoderConfig's main.
evidence: /work/scratch/KubeCoderConfig/CLAUDE.md:19 (every change under kubecoder/ bumps the plugin version)

items.description: §6a — the webhook test ("I want to test this."): review plan §6a's steps ran on the throwaway private repo `pvginkel/jenkins-trigger-test`, with a job created through the API. The result — what a new repo needs for its push hook — is recorded in `report.md` and is the guide's new-repo recipe. The throwaway job is deleted, and deleting the throwaway repo is left to the operator as an action in the close-out report (D4).

Every Jenkins job this slice creates or deletes goes through the API, with its `config.xml` saved under `/work/scratch/jenkins-config/xml/` (a deleted job's under `xml-deleted/`). Every Jenkinsfile the slice writes passes the controller's full declarative linter check.
No existing pipeline is converted: no Jenkinsfile of an existing job changes — `KubeCoder/Jenkinsfile` and ModernAppTemplate's template are untouched — and no library var changes what it does.
No library test coverage is lost: every test class that ran in the library's `kc project test` before this slice still runs and passes.
